title: Etale covers of locally algebraic schemes: dimension and nodal singularities
statement: Let $k$ be an algebraically closed field [def-weil-field, def-weil-algebraic-closure], let $C$ be a locally finite type $k$-scheme [def-pc-scheme, def-weil-finite-type-morphism], and let $(e_i:D_i\to C)_{i\in I}$ be jointly surjective etale morphisms [def-weil-etale-morphism]. Suppose each $D_i$ is locally of finite type over $k$ and $C,D_i$ are locally Noetherian [pqf-def-locnoeth]. For every $i$ and $y\in D_i$, putting $x=e_i(y)$, the local topological dimensions [def-kun-topological-dimension-at-point] satisfy $\dim_yD_i=\dim_xC$. For every $n\in\mathbb N$, $C$ has pure dimension $n$ [def-weil-pure-dimension] if and only if every $D_i$ has pure dimension $n$. Smoothness at $x$ of $C\to\operatorname{Spec}k$ is equivalent to smoothness at $y$ of $D_i\to\operatorname{Spec}k$ [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms]; smoothness at a point means smoothness on an open neighbourhood. If $C$ has pure dimension one (equivalently all the $D_i$ do), then for every such nonsmooth pair $(x,y)$ one has $\widehat{\mathcal O}_{C,x}\cong k[[u,v]]/(uv)$ as complete local $k$-algebras if and only if $\widehat{\mathcal O}_{D_i,y}\cong k[[u,v]]/(uv)$ [def-weil-pbc-adic-completion, def-weil-pbc-multivariate-power-series]. Consequently, under this purity assumption every nonsmooth point of $C$ has the displayed completed local algebra if and only if every nonsmooth point of every $D_i$ does. Completions are taken at maximal ideals. No separatedness or quasi-compactness is required; empty schemes and an empty cover of the empty scheme are included.

proof.text: Fix $i,y$ and put $x=e_i(y)$. By the etale definition $e_i$ is flat and locally finitely presented, hence locally finite type: a finite presentation is in particular a finite generating set. Apply flat-composite fibre-dimension additivity to $D_i\xrightarrow{e_i}C\to\operatorname{Spec}k$. The fibres over the unique point of $\operatorname{Spec}k$ identify with $D_i,C$: the residue-field map there is the identity of $k$, and the fibre-product universal property gives the inverse to each projection. The etale fibre at $x$ has dimension zero at $y$. Thus additivity reads $\dim_yD_i=0+\dim_xC=\dim_xC$. All dimensions here are minima of dimensions of open neighbourhoods.

source.place: Tag 02JS, lemma-dimension-fibre-at-a-point-additive, flat equality; gives the locally algebraic case of descent.tex Tag 04N4

proof.text: For any locally finite type $k$-scheme $Y$ in question, pure dimension $n$ implies $\dim_zY=n$ at every $z$: the component-maximum formula takes the maximum of a nonempty family all equal to $n$. Conversely, if all these local dimensions equal $n$, apply the constant-local-dimension component theorem with $O=Y$; local Noetherianity is assumed. The definition of pure dimension gives the converse. The equality in step 1 therefore transfers purity from $C$ to every $D_i$. In reverse, joint surjectivity supplies a lift $y$ of each $x\in C$, so step 1 makes every $\dim_xC=n$ and the same criterion proves purity of $C$.

source.place: Tag 0A21, lemma-dimension-locally-algebraic (5), component maximum; topology.tex Tags 0052, 0055 for the converse criterion

proof.text: Apply the pointwise assertion of etale-source smoothness to $e_i$ and $C\to\operatorname{Spec}k$. It says exactly that smoothness at $x$ is equivalent to smoothness at $y$. Under pure dimension one, apply nodal-point etale locality to the same map and arbitrary point $y$; its completed-local-$k$-algebra equivalence gives the required nodal equivalence, in particular for every nonsmooth pair.

source.place: Tag 0C5D, lemma-nodal-family-etale-local-source, last sentence; Tag 0C57, lemma-node-etale-local; descent.tex Tag 036U

proof.text: If every nonsmooth point of $C$ has the nodal completion, a nonsmooth $y\in D_i$ has nonsmooth image by step 3, so the nodal equivalence gives its completion. Conversely, lift each nonsmooth $x\in C$ by joint surjectivity; step 3 makes that lift nonsmooth and transfers its nodal completion back to $x$. Empty sources contribute no points. If the covering family is empty, joint surjectivity forces $C$ empty; purity and both universal nodality assertions are then vacuous.
